newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm amid trend uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm amid trend uncertainty.

text.p: Russian MinFin bond prices firmed in thin trading on Monday on mainly local support after tracking a fall in Brady bonds earlier, and dealers said the future trend was unclear.

"Prices started rising in the morning on Moscow support but London was selling on a fall in other emerging markets. But buying has resumed, in London as well," National Reserve Bank dealer Denis Pakhomov said.

Dealers said the market was uncertain as there had been no positive news about President Boris Yeltsin's health and the trend for U.S. Treasuries seemed unclear. Many banks were holding short or flat positions, they added.
Yeltsin's spokesman said on Monday the president was in a stable condition and his temperature normal. He declined to say when Yeltsin, who is suffering from pneumonia, would leave hospital.
"Locals seemed to start strongly today... and MinFins are supported fairly well now. But now Russians are trying to figure out what to do next," a London bank dealer said.
Pakhomov said the current slight upward move could be due to sporadic short-covering, given low trading activity.
